title: Briefing: Albania and India
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Monday, November second. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means only one source has it so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.

Albania. Tirana Mayor Erion Veliaj, held in pre-trial detention on corruption charges he denies, accused Prime Minister Edi Rama of orchestrating his Oct 28 transfer to Fier prison and of using Justice Minister Toni Gogu to demand he give up control of the city, Tirana Times reports. Our grade: disputed. The sides tell it differently, and both versions are on the story page.

India. From October thirty-first: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke said the party backs the INDIA bloc's November first Ramlila Maidan rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar but will not take part, calling the CJP "a neutral platform", Hindustan Times, Outlook India and The Tribune report. We grade that confirmed: Hindustan Times and Outlook India reported it independently.

Also on our watch, with no new reported developments in the last three days: Canada, last reported October thirtieth; Italy, last reported October thirtieth; France, last reported October twenty-seventh; South Africa, last reported October twenty-third. We'll update those as soon as there's news.

The Cockroach Janta Party movement. From October thirty-first: Cockroach Janta Party president Abhijeet Dipke posted an Instagram note to singer Diljit Dosanjh saying he was hurt by the singer's June comments on the protests and asking to end the row, News18, Hindustan Times and The Tribune report. Our grade: confirmed, with independent reporting from Hindustan Times and News18.
Coming up in the days ahead. November fourth, South Africa: local government elections on November fourth.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
